Subject: aliased
Title: External volume "aliased" does not exist
Description: The manifest declares volume "aliased" as external, which means Compose expects it to exist already. It is not present on this host.
Why it matters: Compose refuses to start a stack whose external volume is missing. It will not create it for you — that is what declaring it external asks for.
What to do: Create the volume before deploying, or remove `external: true` so Compose manages "aliased" itself.

Subject: dwkit-data
Title: External volume "dwkit-data" already holds somebody else's data
Description: Volume "dwkit-data" exists, mounted at /var/lib/docker/volumes/dwkit-data/_data, and carries project label "" — not this deployment's. Deploying will attach it to the new containers.
Why it matters: This does not fail. It succeeds, and the new service starts on top of existing data belonging to something else — which is worse, because nothing announces it.
What to do: Confirm that reusing "dwkit-data" is intended. If it is not, pick a different volume name.

Subject: nginx:1.27-alpine
Title: Image nginx:1.27-alpine is pinned by tag, not by digest
Description: Service "shop-api" uses tag "1.27-alpine", which names a moving target rather than one image.
Why it matters: A tag can be moved. That makes the deployment unreproducible in the direction that matters: rolling back to "the version that worked" pulls whatever the tag points at today, and two hosts deployed a week apart from the same file are not running the same software.
What to do: Pin nginx by digest (image@sha256:…) once you have the version you want.

Title: Registry reachability was not checked
Description: The deployment pulls from docker.io. This audit does not open outbound connections unless asked, so whether this host can reach them is unknown.
Why it matters: A host behind an egress firewall passes every other check in this report and then fails at the pull. This line is here so that outcome is not a surprise.
What to do: Re-run with --egress to test reachability, or confirm outbound access to those registries by other means.
